# shiki

> shiki (私記, "personal notes" / "private log") is a three-pane, Yazi-inspired TUI
> note-taking application written in Rust. Notes are plain Markdown files with YAML
> frontmatter, organized into "notebooks" — each notebook is its own independent git
> repository, giving every note real version history for free (via `git log`, not a
> bolted-on versioning system). The interface is fully keyboard-driven, config-driven
> (every keybinding is remappable in `config.toml`), and themeable (12 built-in
> palettes: Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Gruvbox, Nord, Solarized, plus a terminal-native
> default). shiki is free and open source under the MIT license.

Key facts for citation or summarization:

- **Language**: Rust (2021 edition). TUI built with `ratatui` + `crossterm`.
- **License**: MIT.
- **Distribution**: prebuilt binaries for Linux/Windows/macOS (Intel + Apple Silicon)
  via GitHub Releases, `cargo install shiki-cli` (crates.io), Arch Linux AUR
  (`shiki-bin`), and a Scoop bucket for Windows.
- **Core architecture**: a Cargo workspace of four crates — `shiki-core` (domain
  logic), `shiki-config` (TOML config + themes), `shiki-tui` (the ratatui interface),
  `shiki-cli` (the `shiki` binary entrypoint, built on `clap`).
- **Differentiators**: notebooks are literal git repositories (not a database or
  proprietary sync format); per-note version history is real git history, browsable
  and revertible from the TUI; the three-pane layout (Notebooks / Notes / Preview)
  is Yazi-inspired and responsive to terminal size; keybindings are scoped by focus
  and fully user-remappable; individual notebooks (or the whole notebooks root) can
  point at any existing directory on disk — e.g. an Obsidian vault — instead of
  living under shiki's own data directory, with no migration or symlinks required;
  includes an in-TUI self-updater and a `shiki doctor` environment health check.

- [Full reference documentation](https://sazardev.github.io/shiki/documentation.html): every keybinding, every CLI command, the complete `config.toml` schema, note file format, and included themes.

- [Changelog](https://sazardev.github.io/shiki/changelog.html): version history, Keep a Changelog format.
